terra.problem: Verse 13 asks whether Gog has come to take gold; it does not establish that gold is something he has come to grab.
The passage does not mention statues, but that does not establish that there are none.
The passage names Sheba and Dedan separately from the merchants of Tarshish. It also does not say they are watching from the sidelines or establish that none live in the land.
Dwelling securely does not establish that the people feel no fear or are not looking over their shoulders.
The shopping and fair-price joke makes light of Gog's plan to plunder.
A neighbor walking into Papa Dorin's bakery conflicts with his living alone on the cookie planet and inviting bakers by invitation only.
The joke about Gog being honest makes light of his plan to seize plunder.
Papa Dorin claims to have a GPS, adding an outside object to his world rather than discussing it as something people use.
God asks whether Gog is the one spoken of by the earlier prophets. The explanation treats that identification as settled.
The closing sentence merely repeats that God is speaking, leaving the explanation flat and redundant.
The list names particular kinds of creatures and all mankind; saying it includes all living creatures goes beyond the list.
Nothing is left standing goes beyond the mountains, cliffs and walls named in the text.
The verse says every man's sword will be against his brother; it does not identify the men specifically as those with Gog.
The text does not establish that the merchants are excluded from those against whom swords are pointed.
Jonah 1:2 supports that God sent Jonah to Nineveh, but it does not identify him as a prophet. That identification needs a supporting reference.
